summary: Jeffrey Hopkins (1940–2024) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1972, also studying under Geshe Wangyal, Geshe Lhundup Sopa, and the 14th Dalai Lama. He served at the University of Virginia (1973–2005).

Jeffrey J. Kripal (born 1962) specializes in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Conception Seminary College and earned his PhD from the University of Chicago (~1987–1993). Around 2002, he was appointed J. Newton Rayzor Chair at Rice University, which he founded in 2014.

Jeffrey Kotyk is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He earned an MA from Komazawa University and a PhD from Leiden University (ended 2017) under James A. Benn. He held posts at McMaster University (attested 2019) and the University of Bologna.

Jeffrey Mehlman (born 1944) works in philosophy and other fields. He held positions at Cornell, Yale, and Johns Hopkins (~1974–1983), and became University Professor and Professor of French Literature at Boston University around 1983, alongside multiple visiting professorships.

Jeffrey Moussaieff Masson (born 1941) is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He earned his BA and PhD at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He worked at the University of Toronto (1969–1980) and served as Professor of Sanskrit at UC Berkeley (1981–1992).

Jeffrey Newmark is a scholar in Japanology, history, and archaeology. He completed studies at Harvard University (ended 1996) and the University of British Columbia (ended 2009), and held a post at the University of Winnipeg around 2010.

Jeffrey S. Lidke is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He has held academic posts at Berry College and at the University of Virginia, where he was attested as a visiting assistant professor of religion in 2003.

Jeffrey Samuels is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under W. S. Karunatillake and earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Karen Christina Lang (attested 2002). In 2013, he was attested as Associate Professor at Western Kentucky University.

Jeffrey Stout (born 1950) is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Brown University, the California Culinary Academy, and earned his PhD from Princeton University (~1972–1976), where he subsequently served as a professor from 1976 to 2018.

Jeffrey Wayne Bass is a Buddhist studies scholar. He earned degrees from UNC Wilmington, the University of Tennessee, and UCLA, where he completed his PhD under Gregory Schopen. In 2013, he held teaching posts at UCLA and UC San Diego.

Jenkuan Shih is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed graduate education at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, earning an MA supervised by Geshe Lhundup Sopa and a PhD supervised by Charles Hallisey and Mark Csikszentmihalyi.

Jennifer Jung-Kim works in history, archaeology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She held posts at the University of California, Los Angeles, serving as assistant director (attested 2016) and as a lecturer (attested 2026).

Jens Braarvig (born 1948) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held a professorship at the University of Oslo in 2003 and was attested as a professor at the Norwegian Institute of Palaeography and Historical Philology in 2004.

Jens Peter Laut (born 1954) works in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He succeeded Klaus Röhrborn in 2008, held a post at the University of Göttingen (~2008–2021), and serves on the Leitungskommission of the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Jens Schlieter (born 1966) specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Bonn under Josef Simon (~1994–1999) and became Professor for Theory of Religion at the University of Bern around 2009.

Jens-Uwe Hartmann (born 1953) is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his degrees at the University of Munich and completed his habilitation at Göttingen. He was a professor at Humboldt University (1995–2001) and Munich (1999–2018).

Jeong-Eun Kim is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Kim studied under Rosemary Smith and completed a PhD at SOAS University of London by 2011 under the supervision of Youngsook Pak.

Jerome Silbergeld (born 1944) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology. He earned his BA and PhD at Stanford and an MA at Oregon. He held posts at the University of Washington (~1975–2001) and Princeton University (~2001–2018).

Jerzy Bańczerowski (1938–2026) was a Polish linguist. He studied at Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań (~1956–1961), where he later headed the Department of General and Comparative Linguistics (1969) and served as Professor (1977–1991). He was also a Polish Academy of Sciences member.

Jerzy Kuryłowicz (1895–1978) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at the University of Lviv (~1913–1920) and under Antoine Meillet (~1921–1923). He held academic posts at the University of Lviv (~1926–1946) and Jagiellonian University (~1946–1965).
